==English==

===Etymology===
{{bor+|en|ota|بك|tr=bey||gentleman, chief}}, from {{der|en|trk-oat|بك|tr=beg|t=ruler}}, from {{der|en|trk-pro|*bēg|t=lord}}. See there for more.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/beɪ/|a=UK}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-bey.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/bæɪ/|a=[[w:Australian English phonology|AusE]]}}
* {{IPA|en|/beɪ/|a=[[w:General American|GenAm]]}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪ|s=1}}
* {{hmp|en|bay|;|bae<aa:toe-tow>}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|historical}} A governor of a province or district in the [[Turkish]] (e.g. Ottoman) dominions.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1978|author=w:Lawrence Durrell|title=Livia|publisher=Faber & Faber|year_published=1992|series=Avignon Quintet|page=512
|passage=She was chaperoned by the widow of a '''Bey''' whose son had been at Oxford with him, and this gave him the excuse to exchange a few words with her, and then to be presented to the Princess.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=Jon Courtenay Grimwood|title=Pashazade|page=15
|passage=Whether his position with the Third Circle made the difference or the fact that he ranked as a '''bey''', life in El Iskandryia was proving easier than he'd ever dreamed possible when he stepped off the plane.}}
# In various other places, a prince or nobleman.
